mahadasha.Sun: The Sun Mahadasha lasts six years and is the shortest period in the Vimshottari cycle. It brings the themes of self-identity, authority, career standing, relations with the father and with government or institutions, and questions of health and vitality. When the Sun is well placed, dignified and strong by house and sign, the period can raise status, bring recognition from superiors, clarity of purpose, leadership opportunities and a healthier sense of confidence. When the Sun is weak, afflicted by Saturn, Rahu or Ketu, or poorly placed, the same years may bring ego clashes, friction with authority, heart, eye or bone complaints, setbacks in reputation or distance from the father. The classical texts judge results from the Sun's house, sign, aspects and lordships rather than from the planet alone. A constructive attitude is to act with integrity, take responsibility, keep regular routines and honour mentors while avoiding arrogance. Traditional remedies are meant to build humility and discipline.
mahadasha.Moon: The Moon Mahadasha lasts ten years and centres on the mind, emotions, home, mother, public contact, comfort and nourishment. A strong, bright Moon, ideally waxing and well placed, tends to give emotional stability, popularity, good domestic life, property or vehicle gains, support from women and a general sense of peace and prosperity. A weak, waning, eclipsed or afflicted Moon can bring mood swings, anxiety, sleep disturbance, restlessness, changes of residence, strained relations with the mother or fluctuating finances and health, especially digestive or fluid-related problems. Because the Moon changes quickly, this period is often felt as a series of emotional cycles rather than one straight line. The results depend greatly on the Moon's house, its sign dignity, the nakshatra it occupies and the planets aspecting it. Constructive attitude: protect your sleep and routine, cultivate calm company, stay connected with family and avoid decisions made in emotional extremes. Meditation, service to mothers and simple regular habits are the traditional remedial attitude.
mahadasha.Mars: The Mars Mahadasha lasts seven years and is associated with energy, courage, initiative, competition, siblings, land, property, technical skill, surgery and the military or sporting spirit. When Mars is strong and well placed, the native may gain in property, win contests, advance through bold action, receive support from brothers and show real physical stamina and leadership under pressure. When Mars is weak, afflicted or badly placed, the period may bring accidents, inflammation, fevers, blood or surgical issues, quarrels, legal disputes, impatience, litigation over land and strained sibling ties. Mars rewards disciplined action and punishes reckless haste, so the same energy can build or burn depending on how it is used. The chart house of Mars, its dignity and its aspects shape which area is energised. Constructive attitude: channel drive into exercise, skilled work and clear goals, practise patience in speech, avoid risky shortcuts and settle disputes early. Charity, physical discipline and respect for brothers are the traditional remedial approach.
mahadasha.Mercury: The Mercury Mahadasha lasts seventeen years and is a long period of intellect, learning, communication, commerce, writing, analysis, technology and adaptability. With a strong, well placed Mercury, the native often gains in education, business, accounts, teaching, media or advisory work, with sharp reasoning, good networks, humour and flexible skills that create several streams of income. A weak, combust or afflicted Mercury may bring nervous tension, scattered thinking, speech problems, skin or respiratory complaints, miscommunication, business losses, dishonest dealings or indecision. The period often rewards those who keep learning and punishes those who spread themselves too thin. Mercury takes on the colour of the planets it joins, so conjunctions and the house it occupies decide much of its outcome. Constructive attitude: study continuously, keep agreements clear and written, check facts before acting, rest the nervous system and speak truthfully. Service to students, reading, structured routines and honest trade are the traditional remedial attitude.
mahadasha.Jupiter: The Jupiter Mahadasha lasts sixteen years and is regarded as one of the most constructive periods, concerned with wisdom, dharma, teachers, children, wealth, faith, counsel and growth. When Jupiter is strong and well placed, the native may find expansion in knowledge, status, finances and family, with the support of mentors, good fortune, sound judgement, children and a generous, ethical outlook. When Jupiter is weak, afflicted or poorly placed, the period can bring over-optimism, weight or liver issues, poor advice, financial overreach, frustrated education, difficulties with children or loss of faith. Jupiter magnifies whatever it touches, so inflated expectations should be balanced with practical checks. Its results depend on its house, its lordship, its dignity and the aspects it receives. Constructive attitude: seek real teachers, study, give generously within your means, honour promises, and keep humility as things grow. Charity, scripture study and respect for elders and gurus are the traditional remedial attitude.
mahadasha.Venus: The Venus Mahadasha lasts twenty years, the longest of the Vimshottari periods, and concerns love, marriage, partnerships, comfort, wealth, beauty, art, vehicles and refined pleasures. A strong, well placed Venus tends to bring harmonious relationships, material comfort, creative success, social charm, gains through the arts, luxury or hospitality, and a pleasant home life. A weak, combust or afflicted Venus can bring relationship strain, indulgence, reproductive or urinary issues, financial extravagance, scandal, dissatisfaction or confusion over values. Because the period is so long, it usually passes through several phases, shaped by the sub-periods. Its quality depends on Venus's house, sign dignity, aspects and lordship in the chart. Constructive attitude: keep commitments honest, balance enjoyment with discipline, invest in skills and beauty without excess, and treat partners with respect. Gratitude, artistic practice, cleanliness and charity toward women are the traditional remedial attitude.
mahadasha.Saturn: The Saturn Mahadasha lasts nineteen years and is the long, formative period of discipline, responsibility, work, endurance and karmic accounting. With a strong, well placed Saturn, results are slow but durable: steady career growth, authority earned through effort, property, loyal servants or teams, practical wisdom, detachment and lasting achievements. A weak, afflicted or poorly placed Saturn may bring delays, obstacles, isolation, fatigue, joint, bone or chronic ailments, depression, financial restriction, and hard lessons about shortcuts or neglected duties. Saturn tests structure, so those with honest routines tend to pass through it better than those who avoid effort. The house, sign and aspects of Saturn determine where pressure is felt. Constructive attitude: accept responsibility, work patiently, keep commitments, avoid cutting corners, care for the elderly and the poor, and expect rewards to come late but solidly. Service, simplicity and consistent effort are the traditional remedial attitude.
mahadasha.Rahu: The Rahu Mahadasha lasts eighteen years and is a period of ambition, appetite, unconventional paths, foreign links, technology and sudden changes. Rahu acts like the planet it is conjunct or the lord of the sign it occupies, so its results are strongly shaped by placement. When well placed, particularly in the third, sixth, tenth or eleventh houses, it may bring rapid rise, material gains, fame, political or technical success, foreign travel and an ability to break old limits. When afflicted, the period may bring confusion, obsession, deception, anxiety, addictions, unusual illnesses, scandal or abrupt reversals after quick rises. The period often feels restless and unfamiliar. Constructive attitude: stay honest, ground ambitions in ethics, avoid get-rich-quick schemes and intoxicants, verify information, and keep routines that anchor the mind. Charity, mantra practice, service to the marginalised and clear goals are the traditional remedial attitude.
mahadasha.Ketu: The Ketu Mahadasha lasts seven years and is a period of detachment, introspection, past-life tendencies, spiritual interest and sudden endings. Ketu acts through the sign lord and any planets with it, and often removes what is not essential. When well placed, it can give deep insight, intuition, research ability, freedom from attachments, success in healing, occult or specialised study, and liberation from old burdens. When afflicted or poorly placed, it may bring confusion, isolation, sudden losses, mysterious ailments, accidents, loss of interest in worldly goals or a feeling of drifting. Material progress may feel muted even while inner growth deepens. The house Ketu occupies shows where detachment is felt most. Constructive attitude: simplify life, welcome solitude, practise meditation or study, avoid impulsive breaks and keep basic responsibilities in order. Spiritual practice, charity and acceptance of change are the traditional remedial attitude.

Sun.Sun: The Sun-Sun period opens the Sun Mahadasha and shows its pure character: a drive for position, confidence and recognition. Career visibility can rise and relations with the father or superiors come into focus. Heat, pride and strain on the heart or eyes are cautions, so lead with integrity and keep routines steady.
Sun.Moon: The Sun and Moon are natural friends, so this period blends authority with feeling. Public contact, mother, home matters and emotional confidence come forward, and gains through popular support are likely. Moods may sway decisions. Practically, balance ambition with rest, and keep family informed of major plans.
Sun.Mars: The Sun and Mars are friends, giving a spirited, goal-driven period. Courage, competition, property matters and leadership under pressure are highlighted, and decisive action is rewarded. Anger, haste and accidents or fevers are risks. Channel the energy into disciplined projects and avoid confrontations with seniors.
Sun.Mercury: Sun and Mercury are neutral to one another, yet they work well together in practice. Intellect, communication, documents, business and learning come forward, and an authoritative voice helps advisory or administrative work. Nerves and overwork can trouble you. Keep agreements written and check details before committing.
Sun.Jupiter: The Sun and Jupiter are friends, which makes this one of the kindlier sub-periods. Guidance from mentors, ethical leadership, advancement, children and religious or educational interests are favoured, along with improved prosperity. Over-optimism is the risk. Use the support to build lasting foundations rather than to expand too quickly.
Sun.Venus: The Sun and Venus are adversaries, so authority and pleasure pull in different directions. Relationships, money, comforts and creative matters are active, but ego clashes with partners or lowered vitality can arise. Practically, keep spending measured, give a partner space and avoid mixing business with romance.
Sun.Saturn: The Sun and Saturn are enemies, producing a demanding period of duty against ambition. Delays, workload, friction with superiors and the father, and bone, joint or heart concerns can arise. Long-term effort still builds credibility. Practically, plan patiently, honour responsibilities and avoid dramatic moves against authority.
Sun.Rahu: Rahu in a Sun period blends status ambition with sudden, unconventional events. Foreign links, politics, technology and rapid changes of position may appear, together with confusion or eclipse-like reversals. Practically, verify claims, avoid shortcuts, protect health and keep your reputation clean while pursuing advancement.
Sun.Ketu: Ketu in a Sun period turns authority inward, bringing detachment from status and questions about purpose. Spiritual interest, research and simplified goals can grow, while career setbacks, disputes with superiors or sudden endings may occur. Practically, stay flexible, finish obligations cleanly and treat any loss of position as a prompt to refine your direction.

Moon.Sun: The Moon regards the Sun as a friend, so this sub-period supports confidence in a feeling-led decade. Recognition, career steadiness, clarity about purpose and improved ties with the father or authority are likely. Pride may sensitise the mind. Practically, use the clarity to set direction and keep emotional reactions out of professional matters.
Moon.Moon: The Moon-Moon period opens the Moon Mahadasha and shows it in pure form: emotional tides, home, mother, public contact and comforts. Popularity and domestic happiness come when the Moon is strong, anxiety and changes of residence when weak. Practically, protect sleep, keep a gentle routine and avoid deciding in mood swings.
Moon.Mars: The Moon is neutral toward Mars, which here brings emotional energy and drive. Property, siblings, assertive action and domestic projects are active, and courage grows, though irritability, arguments and fevers can follow. Practically, channel feelings into exercise and building work, and postpone confrontations until calm.
Moon.Mercury: The Moon is friendly toward Mercury, favouring a lively and communicative period. Learning, trade, writing, travel and social networks flourish, and the mind feels agile. Nervousness and overthinking can unsettle sleep. Practically, use the momentum for study and commerce, keep records clear and give the mind rest.
Moon.Jupiter: The Moon is neutral toward Jupiter, though this blend is traditionally gentle and fortunate. Wisdom, family blessings, children, teachers, devotion and financial growth come forward, and the mind finds peace. Over-comfort or excess weight are mild risks. Practically, invest in learning, support dependants and give generously within means.
Moon.Venus: The Moon is neutral toward Venus, and together they emphasise comfort and affection. Marriage, relationships, art, luxuries, vehicles and finances are active, and emotional enjoyment is high. Indulgence, attachment and fluid-related health concerns may follow. Practically, enjoy refinement, set a budget and keep relationships honest.
Moon.Saturn: The Moon is neutral toward Saturn, yet their contrast weighs on the mind. Duties, delays, loneliness, fatigue and worry may surface, especially around the mother or home. Long-term discipline can still stabilise the emotions. Practically, keep a regular routine, seek supportive company and avoid brooding or neglecting health.
Moon.Rahu: Rahu in a Moon period amplifies emotion with ambition, producing restlessness, cravings, vivid imagination and unusual contacts. Foreign links or media-related gains are possible, as are anxiety, confusion and sleep disturbance. Practically, avoid intoxicants, verify information, keep a stable routine and do not act on sudden fears.
Moon.Ketu: Ketu in a Moon period draws feeling inward, creating detachment, intuition and spiritual curiosity. Emotional withdrawal, loss of interest in comforts, solitude and unexplained worries may also appear. Practically, welcome meditation and quiet reflection, stay connected with trusted people and avoid sudden, irreversible emotional decisions.

Mars.Sun: Mars and the Sun are friends, giving a confident, forceful period. Leadership, career advancement, authority and vitality increase, and decisive action is respected. Pride, fever, inflammation and clashes with seniors are cautions. Practically, take initiative on worthwhile projects and keep temper and ego under supervision.
Mars.Moon: Mars regards the Moon as a friend, which warms action with feeling. Property, home improvements, family protection and public activity are favoured, and gains through land or women can arise. Emotional impulsiveness and domestic irritation are risks. Practically, act on practical plans and keep sensitive discussions calm.
Mars.Mars: The Mars-Mars period opens the Mars Mahadasha, showing its energy in full: courage, competition, property and technical drive. Strong Mars brings achievement and vigour, weak Mars accidents, anger and disputes. Practically, take regular exercise, handle legal and land matters carefully and avoid risky speed.
Mars.Mercury: Mars and Mercury are enemies, so energy and intellect strain against one another. Debate, business, technical work and communication are active, but sharp speech, nervous tension, rash contracts and quarrels may occur. Practically, think before speaking, write agreements down and use the energy for skilled, detailed work.
Mars.Jupiter: Mars and Jupiter are friends, so action is guided by wisdom. Advancement, property gains, legal success, religious or educational pursuits and support from elders are favoured, and courage serves ideals. Overconfidence is the risk. Practically, use good counsel for major moves and direct strength toward constructive causes.
Mars.Venus: Mars is neutral toward Venus, and the pair mixes desire with drive. Romance, marriage, vehicles, finances and creative ventures become active, with passion rising. Quarrels over affection, impulsive spending and reproductive or urinary concerns are possible. Practically, keep commitments honest and avoid mixing temper with intimacy.
Mars.Saturn: Mars is neutral toward Saturn, yet this is a hard, disciplined mix of heat and restraint. Heavy work, delays, obstacles, accidents or surgeries, and strained labour relations may occur, though technical and engineering effort pays off slowly. Practically, work patiently, be careful with machinery and travel, and avoid forcing outcomes.
Mars.Rahu: Rahu in a Mars period intensifies courage into daring, sometimes reckless ambition. Technology, risk, foreign ventures or sudden conflicts may rise, along with accidents, anger, deception or legal problems. Practically, keep safety first, avoid impulsive confrontation, verify partners and aim intensity at disciplined goals.
Mars.Ketu: Ketu in a Mars period turns fire into sharp, withdrawn focus. Surgery, technical research, spiritual discipline and detachment from conflict may appear, but accidents, sudden separations and lost motivation are cautions. Practically, take safety precautions, simplify goals and use solitary discipline rather than battle to make progress.

Mercury.Sun: Mercury regards the Sun as a friend, which gives intellect authority. Recognition at work, administrative or advisory roles, clearer purpose and support from superiors are likely. Pride in opinions and overwork can follow. Practically, step into leadership of projects, present ideas confidently and watch eyes, nerves and stress.
Mercury.Moon: Mercury and the Moon are enemies in classical terms, so logic and feeling pull apart. Learning, public dealings, travel and home concerns are active, but anxiety, indecision, mood-driven speech and sleep disturbance may appear. Practically, keep a calm routine, avoid contracts signed in a mood and talk things over before deciding.
Mercury.Mars: Mercury is neutral toward Mars, but this mix is brisk and technical. Engineering, debate, sales, competitive study and property papers come forward, and quick thinking is rewarded. Sharp words, haste and nervous irritation are risks. Practically, check technical details twice and keep arguments out of business.
Mercury.Mercury: The Mercury-Mercury period opens the Mercury Mahadasha, showing learning, trade, communication and analysis in clear form. Skill and income can grow through study and networking when Mercury is strong, while nervous strain and mixed messages appear when weak. Practically, keep studying, keep records tidy and rest the mind.
Mercury.Jupiter: Mercury is neutral toward Jupiter, though together they favour higher learning and wise commerce. Education, teaching, publishing, advice, finances and children are active, and judgement matures. Over-planning or excess talk can dilute results. Practically, pursue qualifications, seek mentors and put knowledge into sound action.
Mercury.Venus: Mercury and Venus are friends, making this a pleasant, productive sub-period. Art, design, entertainment, relationships, trade and finance improve, and charm aids negotiation. Light-minded spending and flirtation are cautions. Practically, use social skill for business, invest in creative skills and keep commitments clear.
Mercury.Saturn: Mercury is neutral toward Saturn, yet the two cooperate on structured, disciplined thought. Research, accounts, law, administration and long-term study progress steadily, though delays, worry and fatigue are possible. Practically, accept slower pace, organise records and build durable skills instead of seeking quick wins.
Mercury.Rahu: Rahu in a Mercury period amplifies cleverness and curiosity. Technology, media, trade, foreign contacts and unconventional learning may flourish, while deceit, over-speculation, nervous overload and misinformation are risks. Practically, verify facts and contracts, avoid get-rich-quick plans and give the nervous system real rest.
Mercury.Ketu: Ketu in a Mercury period turns the mind inward, supporting research, intuition, astrology, spiritual study and detachment from chatter. Confusion in communication, lost interest in business and sudden changes in studies can arise. Practically, work quietly on specialised knowledge, keep written records and avoid important decisions when uncertain.

Jupiter.Sun: Jupiter regards the Sun as a friend, so wisdom meets authority. Recognition, leadership, government or institutional support, improved standing with the father and mentors, and clearer purpose are favoured. Pride may creep in. Practically, accept responsibility, share credit and use influence to support teaching, ethics and long-term projects.
Jupiter.Moon: Jupiter regards the Moon as a friend, giving a warm, prosperous sub-period. Family happiness, home, mother, children, public goodwill, devotion and financial comfort are favoured, and the mind finds peace. Complacency and weight gain are mild cautions. Practically, strengthen family bonds, give to worthy causes and keep healthy habits.
Jupiter.Mars: Jupiter regards Mars as a friend, which turns wisdom into action. Property, courage, siblings, legal wins, advancement and decisive projects are favoured, with support from elders. Impatience and overconfidence are cautions. Practically, act on well-considered plans, protect health through exercise and use energy for principled goals.
Jupiter.Mercury: Jupiter and Mercury are enemies in classical terms, so wisdom and cleverness can disagree. Study, trade, writing and communication are active, but mixed advice, scattered effort, disputes over details or nervous strain may arise. Practically, verify facts, seek balanced counsel and commit to one clear plan.
Jupiter.Jupiter: The Jupiter-Jupiter period opens the Jupiter Mahadasha, showing growth, wisdom, children, teachers and prosperity in pure form. A strong Jupiter brings fortune and honour, while a weak one brings over-optimism and misjudgement. Practically, study, give generously, honour promises and let expansion stay disciplined by humility.
Jupiter.Venus: Jupiter and Venus are adversaries, so wisdom and pleasure compete. Marriage, finance, arts, luxury and comfort are active, but indulgence, relationship disagreements and lax discipline can reduce results. Practically, enjoy prosperity with moderation, keep principles in partnerships and invest in lasting value rather than display.
Jupiter.Saturn: Jupiter is neutral toward Saturn, and the two balance expansion with restraint. Career responsibility, institutional work, delayed but durable gains, and mature wisdom are indicated, while workload, slow progress and chronic health concerns are cautions. Practically, build patiently, support elders and aim for sustainable growth.
Jupiter.Rahu: Rahu in a Jupiter period mixes tradition with unorthodox growth. Foreign travel, unusual teachers, technology, publishing and rapid gains may arise, alongside confusion about beliefs, bad advice or moral compromise. Practically, check the integrity of mentors and ventures, stay ethical and avoid excessive speculation.
Jupiter.Ketu: Ketu in a Jupiter period favours spiritual depth. Meditation, philosophy, pilgrimage, renunciation and subtle insight can grow, while detachment from worldly ambition, weak finances or conflict with teachers may follow. Practically, honour practice, keep essential responsibilities in order and let simplicity shape the use of wealth.

Venus.Sun: Venus and the Sun are adversaries, so pleasure and prestige clash. Career visibility, relations with authority and finances are active, but ego conflicts with partners, heat in the body and reduced harmony can arise. Practically, avoid mixing power struggles with romance, spend measuredly and focus on steady work over display.
Venus.Moon: Venus and the Moon are adversaries in classical terms, though both love comfort. Home, women, relationships, vehicles and emotional enjoyment are active, with sensitivity and mood changes. Over-attachment, indulgence and fluid-related health issues are cautions. Practically, create a pleasant home, keep boundaries clear and avoid emotional spending.
Venus.Mars: Venus is neutral toward Mars, and together they raise passion and drive. Romance, marriage, property, vehicles and creative enterprise are active, and desire is strong. Quarrels, impulsive spending, and reproductive or urinary complaints are risks. Practically, channel energy into building shared goals and avoid jealous reactions.
Venus.Mercury: Venus and Mercury are friends, making this an agreeable, productive sub-period. Art, design, trade, writing, social life and finances improve, and charm aids negotiation. Light spending and scattered flirtation are small risks. Practically, develop creative skills, use communication for business and keep promises clear.
Venus.Jupiter: Venus is neutral toward Jupiter, and together they favour refinement with wisdom. Marriage, children, teaching, finance, devotion and prosperity are favoured, and the outlook is generous. Over-comfort and weight gain are cautions. Practically, invest in lasting values, support dependants and enjoy abundance with discipline.
Venus.Venus: The Venus-Venus period opens the Venus Mahadasha, bringing love, comfort, wealth, art and partnerships in pure form. A strong Venus gives harmony and success, while a weak one gives strain and indulgence. Practically, cultivate honest relationships, enjoy refinement in moderation and save as well as spend.
Venus.Saturn: Venus and Saturn are friends, so pleasure matures into steady commitment. Career, property, long-term relationships, business discipline and finances can grow reliably, though delays and a serious mood are possible. Practically, build slowly, honour commitments, work consistently and accept that results come with patience.
Venus.Rahu: Rahu in a Venus period amplifies desire and ambition. Glamour, media, foreign relationships, luxury and rapid financial changes may appear, along with scandal, obsession, deception in partnerships and unusual health issues. Practically, keep relationships honest, verify financial dealings and limit indulgence.
Venus.Ketu: Ketu in a Venus period brings detachment from pleasure. Spiritual interests, simplified tastes and subtle creativity may grow, while relationship distance, loss of interest in comforts, or sudden separations can arise. Practically, communicate with partners, avoid abrupt breaks and treat withdrawal as an invitation to refine values.

Saturn.Sun: Saturn and the Sun are enemies, so duty and authority clash. Career responsibility, relations with superiors and the father, and health are tested, with delays, friction and fatigue possible. Still, disciplined leadership can earn lasting credibility. Practically, avoid power struggles, honour commitments and care for heart, bones and eyes.
Saturn.Moon: Saturn and the Moon are enemies in classical texts, so heaviness weighs on feeling. Worry, loneliness, domestic strain, the mother's health and fluctuating finances may arise, though emotional maturity can grow. Practically, keep a regular routine, seek supportive company, and avoid brooding or isolating yourself.
Saturn.Mars: Saturn and Mars are enemies, giving a forceful, frustrating sub-period. Hard work, technical or construction projects, property matters, accidents, conflicts and surgeries are possible. Patience matters more than speed. Practically, plan safety, avoid rash confrontations and apply sustained effort to demanding, skilled work.
Saturn.Mercury: Saturn and Mercury are friends, so thought and discipline cooperate. Study, accounts, law, trade, administration and technical work progress steadily, and judgement matures. Worry and nervous fatigue are cautions. Practically, organise records, commit to long-term learning and build skills that endure.
Saturn.Jupiter: Saturn is neutral toward Jupiter, though this sub-period brings relief and wisdom. Mentors, children, higher learning, stable gains and ethical responsibility are favoured, and obstacles ease gradually. Practically, take advice, expand conservatively and use the improvement to strengthen foundations.
Saturn.Venus: Saturn and Venus are friends, softening a hard dasha with comfort. Marriage, property, vehicles, career in the arts or luxury, and financial stability improve, with loyalty to commitments. Complacency and indulgence are minor risks. Practically, build assets sensibly and maintain relationships through steady attention.
Saturn.Saturn: The Saturn-Saturn period opens the Saturn Mahadasha and shows its discipline, delay and responsibility most clearly. Strong Saturn rewards patient work, while weak Saturn brings obstacles, fatigue and isolation. Practically, accept duty, avoid shortcuts, keep routines and expect durable results to come slowly.
Saturn.Rahu: Rahu in a Saturn period intensifies ambition, delay and unconventional pressures. Foreign work, technology and large organisations may bring progress, but confusion, anxiety, deception, chronic complaints and sudden setbacks are possible. Practically, keep ethics steady, avoid shortcuts and verify agreements carefully.
Saturn.Ketu: Ketu in a Saturn period encourages renunciation and austerity. Spiritual discipline, solitary research and simplified living may flourish, while isolation, lack of motivation, joint or nerve complaints and sudden detachment from responsibilities are possible. Practically, keep duties in order and treat solitude as a place for steady practice.

Rahu.Sun: Rahu is inimical to the Sun, so ambition collides with authority. Career, government, the father and prestige are active, with eclipse-like swings between recognition and obstruction. Ego clashes and heat in the body are risks. Practically, work transparently, respect superiors and avoid risky shortcuts to status.
Rahu.Moon: Rahu is inimical to the Moon, so the mind becomes restless and imaginative. Home, mother, public image, foreign residence and emotional matters are active, with anxiety, cravings and sleep trouble possible. Practically, keep strict routines, avoid intoxicants, rest the mind and delay big choices made in fear.
Rahu.Mars: Rahu is inimical to Mars, creating a high-voltage, risk-prone mix. Courage, technical ambition, property and competition surge, along with accidents, anger, legal trouble and sudden disputes. Practically, prioritise safety, curb impulsive confrontation, verify partners and channel intensity into disciplined projects.
Rahu.Mercury: Rahu and Mercury are friends, giving sharp, inventive thinking. Technology, media, trade, research, writing and foreign dealings can flourish, and learning accelerates. Nervous overload, deceit and over-speculation are risks. Practically, verify information, document agreements and rest the mind regularly.
Rahu.Jupiter: Rahu is neutral toward Jupiter, and the blend mixes tradition with unorthodox growth. Higher education, foreign teachers, finances, children and spiritual curiosity are active, and fortune can improve. Questionable advice and moral compromise are risks. Practically, check mentors' integrity and expand gradually.
Rahu.Venus: Rahu and Venus are friends, which is often a pleasant, worldly sub-period. Glamour, relationships, luxury, art, media and finance can bring gains, with strong desire. Indulgence, scandal and unusual relationships are cautions. Practically, keep promises, manage money plainly and limit excess.
Rahu.Saturn: Rahu and Saturn are friends, so ambition meets discipline. Career building, organisations, technical or foreign work and long-term projects advance, though delays, anxiety and sustained pressure are likely. Practically, work consistently, avoid dishonest shortcuts and protect health from stress.
Rahu.Rahu: The Rahu-Rahu period opens the Rahu Mahadasha and shows its character most plainly: hunger for advancement, unusual circumstances and sudden shifts. Gains and confusion can mix. Practically, set ethical goals, avoid get-rich-quick offers and stay grounded with regular habits while chasing ambition.
Rahu.Ketu: Rahu and Ketu form one axis, so desire alternates with detachment. Sudden separations, spiritual questions, strange health complaints, lost direction and karmic turns are possible, along with unusual insight. Practically, keep life simple, stay with a steady practice and avoid irreversible decisions in confusion.

Ketu.Sun: Ketu is inimical to the Sun, so detachment meets the wish for recognition. Career, status, the father and self-image are questioned, with disputes with authority, health strain or sudden role changes possible. Practically, accept a quieter position, refine purpose and avoid power struggles.
Ketu.Moon: Ketu is inimical to the Moon, so the inner world turns unsettled and subtle. Home, mother, sleep and emotional security are tested, though intuition and spiritual receptivity deepen. Practically, maintain a gentle routine, meditate, stay in touch with trusted people and avoid isolating yourself.
Ketu.Mars: Ketu is friendly toward Mars, which gives focused, sharp energy. Technical work, surgery, research, spiritual discipline and property matters can progress, though accidents, injuries, sudden quarrels and impatience are cautions. Practically, take safety measures and use concentrated effort for specific goals.
Ketu.Mercury: Ketu is neutral toward Mercury, and the mix favours intuitive, research-minded thinking. Specialised study, astrology, analysis and quiet writing progress, while confusion in communication, scattered studies or lost interest in trade may occur. Practically, keep records, focus on one subject and verify understandings.
Ketu.Jupiter: Ketu is neutral toward Jupiter, yet this sub-period supports spiritual insight. Meditation, philosophy, pilgrimage, mentoring and inner learning are favoured, with detachment from material gain. Conflict with teachers or financial vagueness is possible. Practically, follow genuine practice, keep basic obligations and give simply.
Ketu.Venus: Ketu is friendly toward Venus, softening detachment with refinement. Subtle art, devotional life, quiet relationships and simple comforts can grow, while loss of interest in pleasure or relationship distance may arise. Practically, communicate honestly with partners and enjoy modest, meaningful comforts.
Ketu.Saturn: Ketu is friendly toward Saturn, producing an austere, enduring sub-period. Discipline, solitude, service, research and spiritual practice can mature, while delays, fatigue, nerve or joint concerns and lowered motivation are possible. Practically, keep routines, serve quietly and be patient with slow progress.
Ketu.Rahu: Ketu and Rahu form one axis, so detachment mixes with sudden appetite. Unexpected changes, foreign matters, confusion, strange ailments and karmic turning points may arise, along with unusual insight. Practically, keep life uncluttered, avoid hasty commitments and rely on steady spiritual or health routines.
Ketu.Ketu: The Ketu-Ketu period opens the Ketu Mahadasha and shows its detachment, introspection and sudden endings most plainly. Clearing old burdens and spiritual progress can come with confusion and loss of interest in worldly goals. Practically, simplify, practise meditation, finish obligations and avoid abrupt, irreversible breaks.

Sun.Aries: The Sun is exalted in Aries, most strongly near ten degrees. The classics describe a courageous, energetic, famous and commanding person, quick to act, fond of travel and conquest, and capable of leading armies or institutions. Anger and impatience can arise, and the person may be restless. Support from rulers and a good reputation are promised when the house is sound.

Rahu.Capricorn: Rahu in Capricorn is in the friendly sign of Saturn. The texts describe a highly ambitious, practical and strategic person, capable of building power, business or political influence through persistence and unconventional methods. Career focus is strong. Coldness, ruthlessness or workaholism are risks, while discipline and clear ethics make this an effective placement for worldly success.
Rahu.Aquarius: Rahu in Aquarius is often regarded as being in its own sign, as co-ruler with Saturn. The classics describe an innovative, humanitarian and technologically gifted person, gaining through networks, science, media and large organisations, with an unusual social circle. Detachment and rebellious ideas are possible. The placement supports original contribution when guided by service.
Rahu.Pisces: Rahu in Pisces is in the sign of Jupiter, a neutral placement. The texts describe an imaginative, dreamy and spiritually curious person, drawn to mysticism, foreign lands, film, healing or institutions, with strong intuition but a tendency toward illusion. Boundaries and addictions need care. Grounded faith, creative outlets and honest routines bring useful results.

Ketu.Aries: Ketu in Aries lies in the friendly sign of Mars. The classics describe a courageous but inwardly detached person, with a strong instinct for action, sharp intuition, and an interest in martial, surgical or spiritual discipline. Identity can feel unclear, and impulsive decisions or accidents are cautions. The placement favours quiet, self-reliant courage over display.
Ketu.Taurus: Ketu is considered debilitated in Taurus, in the sign of Venus. The texts describe detachment from possessions, uneasy finances, strained family speech and unusual relations with comfort, food or wealth, though also contentment with little. Material security needs conscious attention. Simplicity, honest speech and careful budgeting help, and spiritual value can emerge from renunciation.
Ketu.Gemini: Ketu in Gemini is considered weak in some Parashari views, in the sign of Mercury. The classics describe a restless, intuitive but uncertain mind, with difficulty trusting words, schooling or logic, yet flashes of insight and an interest in hidden knowledge. Communication may be misunderstood. Grounded study, clear writing and patience steady the nerves.
Ketu.Cancer: Ketu in Cancer lies in the sign of the Moon, an adversary. Traditional descriptions give a reserved, sensitive person with detachment from home, mother or emotional ties, deep inner feeling that is hard to voice, and possible changes of residence. Anxiety and sleep disturbance may arise. Meditation, compassion and a quiet daily rhythm give emotional steadiness.
Ketu.Leo: Ketu in Leo is in the sign of the Sun, an adversary. The texts describe a person indifferent to fame and status, with an independent, introspective pride, difficulty with authority or the father, and a search for spiritual authority within. Ego issues and heart or vitality concerns may arise. Service without recognition brings the greatest satisfaction.
Ketu.Virgo: Ketu in Virgo lies in a neutral sign of Mercury. The classics describe an analytic, intuitive and discreet person, skilled in healing, research, occult sciences or meticulous service, with a critical inner voice. Worry and perfectionism can be heavy. Practical routines, humility and helpful work make this a useful placement for specialised knowledge.
Ketu.Libra: Ketu in Libra is in the friendly sign of Venus. The texts describe a detached, fair-minded and quietly refined person, with unusual attitudes to partnership, marriage and business, who values freedom and may attract karmic relationships. Indecision and withdrawal can interfere with cooperation. Honest communication and spiritual perspective keep relationships healthy.
Ketu.Scorpio: Ketu is exalted in Scorpio in the commonly accepted view, in the sign of Mars. The classics describe a deep, intuitive and fearless person, with strong occult, psychological or healing ability, penetrating insight, and freedom from attachment to fear. Crises become initiations. Secretiveness and a sharp temper are cautions, while research and spiritual practice flourish.
Ketu.Sagittarius: Ketu in Sagittarius is considered exalted in some Parashari views, in the sign of Jupiter. The texts describe a mystical, philosophical and intuitive person, drawn to renunciation, ancient teachings and inner truth rather than dogma, with detachment from formal belief. Teachers may be unconventional. Lack of direction is a risk, while wisdom through experience is likely.
Ketu.Capricorn: Ketu in Capricorn lies in the friendly sign of Saturn. The classics describe a quiet, disciplined and detached worker, indifferent to status yet capable of deep concentration and technical mastery, with possible delays or reversals in career. Responsibility is carried without display. Patience, humble service and practical spirituality bring stability.
Ketu.Aquarius: Ketu in Aquarius is in the friendly sign of Saturn. The texts describe an original, detached and intuitive person, interested in science, mysticism, and humanitarian ideals, with few but significant friendships. Social ambition is muted. Isolation or eccentric views are cautions, while innovation and service to a larger cause give meaning.
Ketu.Pisces: Ketu in Pisces is regarded as in its own sign in some traditions, in the sign of Jupiter. The classics describe a deeply spiritual, compassionate and intuitive person, drawn to meditation, solitude, renunciation, healing or ashram life, with psychic sensitivity. Boundaries and practicality can slip. Regular practice and grounded service allow moksha-oriented gifts to mature.

tithi.Shukla Pratipada: Ruled by Agni, this first day of the bright fortnight is a Nanda tithi. Natives tend to be determined, self-reliant and quick to start things, with a fiery pride. It suits beginnings and enterprise, though stubbornness and impatience should be tempered.
tithi.Shukla Dwitiya: Ruled by Brahma, the creator, Dwitiya is a Bhadra tithi of building and steady growth. Natives are constructive, dutiful and fond of family and home, and often skilled at laying foundations. It suits ceremonies, construction and nurturing projects.
tithi.Shukla Tritiya: Ruled by Gauri, Tritiya is a Jaya tithi of grace and victory. Natives are charming, artistic and devout, with perseverance that wins through skill rather than force. Good for worship, arts, marriage preparations and beginning skilled work.
tithi.Shukla Chaturthi: Ruled by Ganesha, remover of obstacles, Chaturthi is a Rikta tithi, considered empty for new ventures. Natives are practical and clever, often skilled at solving problems, though they may meet struggle first. Best used to remove hurdles and worship Ganesha.
tithi.Shukla Panchami: Ruled by the Nagas, Panchami is a Purna tithi of fulfilment. Natives are intelligent, learned and healing-minded, with interest in medicine, study and subtle knowledge. It supports education, remedies, and reconciliation, and rewards quiet persistence.
tithi.Shukla Shashthi: Ruled by Kartikeya, the divine commander, Shashthi is a Nanda tithi. Natives are brave, disciplined and protective, with an athletic or martial bent and a clear sense of duty. It suits training, competition, and starting energetic work.
tithi.Shukla Saptami: Ruled by Surya, Saptami is a Bhadra tithi of vitality and light. Natives are radiant, active and respected, with leadership, a liking for travel and a good constitution. It is favourable for journeys, vehicles, healing and public undertakings.
tithi.Shukla Ashtami: Ruled by Rudra, Ashtami is a Jaya tithi of intensity. Natives are strong-willed, transformative and sometimes combative, with sharp ups and downs and deep resolve. It favours worship of Shiva and Durga, discipline and bold, focused effort.
tithi.Shukla Navami: Ruled by Durga, Navami is a Rikta tithi of power. Natives are courageous, protective and fiercely determined, with a strong sense of justice and a tendency to clash. It is potent for strength and defence but not for gentle new ventures.
tithi.Shukla Dashami: Ruled by Dharmaraja Yama, Dashami is a Purna tithi of righteousness. Natives are dutiful, honest and steady, succeeding through lawful effort and a firm sense of ethics. It supports undertakings of long duration, public work and travel.
tithi.Shukla Ekadashi: Ruled by the Vishvedevas, Ekadashi is a Nanda tithi sacred to Vishnu worship and fasting. Natives are devoted, generous and self-disciplined, with a pure, contemplative streak. It favours spiritual practice, charity and sincere new beginnings.
tithi.Shukla Dwadashi: Ruled by Vishnu, Dwadashi is a Bhadra tithi of preservation. Natives are calm, charitable and religious, valuing ritual, truth and family harmony. It suits breaking fasts, giving, ceremonies and quietly consolidating gains.
tithi.Shukla Trayodashi: Ruled by Kamadeva, Trayodashi is a Jaya tithi of desire and charm. Natives are attractive, sociable and pleasure-loving, with a warm magnetic presence and artistic taste. It suits romance, beautification, entertainment and social ventures.
tithi.Shukla Chaturdashi: Ruled by Shiva, Chaturdashi is a Rikta tithi of strong, concentrated energy. Natives are bold, fierce-spirited and ascetic in streak, with sharp temper and powerful will. It is better for worship, austerity and breaking obstacles than for gentle new starts.
tithi.Purnima: Purnima, the full-moon day, is ruled by the Moon. A birth here gives emotional fullness, public appeal, creativity and generosity, with a strong mind that can feel tides of emotion. It is a day of worship, completion and abundance.
tithi.Krishna Pratipada: Ruled by Agni, the first day after the full moon is a Nanda tithi. Natives are self-possessed, thoughtful and independent, with initiative that works quietly rather than boldly. It suits consolidation, study and modest restarts more than grand openings.
tithi.Krishna Dwitiya: Ruled by Brahma, Dwitiya is a Bhadra tithi of steady work. Natives are dutiful, practical and family-minded, building security patiently and without display. It favours home improvements, quiet construction and careful planning.
tithi.Krishna Tritiya: Ruled by Gauri, Tritiya is a Jaya tithi of grace under pressure. Natives are artistic, devout and resourceful, with quiet strength that prevails in difficulty. It supports worship, craft and solving matters gently.
tithi.Krishna Chaturthi: Ruled by Ganesha, Chaturthi is a Rikta tithi, with Sankashti observance for removing obstacles. Natives are inventive, resilient and sceptical, learning through trial. It suits vows, problem solving and clearing blocks rather than new ventures.
tithi.Krishna Panchami: Ruled by the Nagas, Panchami is a Purna tithi. Natives are observant, wise and healing-minded, with interest in subtle knowledge and hidden matters. It supports study, remedies, and careful completion of ongoing work.
tithi.Krishna Shashthi: Ruled by Kartikeya, Shashthi is a Nanda tithi. Natives are disciplined, protective and tenacious, with a soldierly sense of duty that works without applause. It suits practice, endurance training and firm, behind-the-scenes effort.
tithi.Krishna Saptami: Ruled by Surya, Saptami is a Bhadra tithi. Natives are dignified, self-reliant and health-conscious, with steady leadership more than showmanship. It is suitable for travel, treatment and gradual public work, but not for grand launches.
tithi.Krishna Ashtami: Ruled by Rudra, Ashtami is a Jaya tithi, associated with Krishna's birth in many traditions. Natives are intense, devoted and transformative, with deep inner strength and some turbulence. It favours devotion, discipline and surmounting rivals.
tithi.Krishna Navami: Ruled by Durga, Navami is a Rikta tithi. Natives are brave, protective and independent, with fierce resolve under strain and a tendency toward conflict. It supports defence and perseverance but is poor for tender new beginnings.
tithi.Krishna Dashami: Ruled by Dharmaraja, Dashami is a Purna tithi. Natives are principled, steady and quietly capable, succeeding through duty and fair dealing. It suits completing responsibilities, legal tidiness and ethical work.
tithi.Krishna Ekadashi: Ruled by the Vishvedevas, Ekadashi is a Nanda tithi, sacred for Vishnu worship and fasting. Natives are devout, pure-hearted and charitable, with an introspective, self-disciplined temperament. It favours spiritual vows, giving and inner work.
tithi.Krishna Dwadashi: Ruled by Vishnu, Dwadashi is a Bhadra tithi. Natives are calm, giving and traditional, with steady faith and moderated desires. It supports charity, ritual observance and quiet stabilising of affairs.
tithi.Krishna Trayodashi: Ruled by Kamadeva, Trayodashi is a Jaya tithi, with Pradosha worship of Shiva in this fortnight. Natives are charming, sensual and appealing, though more reserved than in the bright half. It suits devotion, art and gentle social matters.
tithi.Krishna Chaturdashi: Ruled by Shiva, Chaturdashi is a Rikta tithi, the day of Masik Shivaratri. Natives are fearless, austere and drawn to the mystical, with sharp temper and deep resolve. It suits introspection, penance and Shiva worship, not new ventures.
tithi.Amavasya: Amavasya, the new-moon day, is ruled by the ancestors. A birth here suggests introspection, a reserved temperament and strong ancestral karma. It is poor for new ventures but excellent for ancestral rites, reflection, inner work and quiet resolve.

yoga.Vishkambha: Vishkambha, ruled by Yama, is considered a difficult yoga. It may give obstacles early in life, a stubborn, proud nature and strain in health or relationships, though discipline and patience turn it into resilience. Auspicious beginnings are best avoided.
yoga.Priti: Priti, ruled by Vishnu, means affection. A birth here gives a loving, likable and cooperative nature with talent in relationships and a good capacity for friendship. It is auspicious and supports harmony, gifts, creative pursuits and agreements.
yoga.Ayushman: Ayushman, ruled by the Moon, relates to longevity. It tends to give good health, resilience, stability and a long life, along with a pleasant, cheerful temperament. It is favourable for health matters and for beginnings that need endurance.
yoga.Saubhagya: Saubhagya, ruled by Brahma, means good fortune. It tends to give a lucky, comfortable and pleasant life, charm, harmonious relationships and domestic happiness. It supports weddings, celebrations and pleasant undertakings.
yoga.Shobhana: Shobhana, ruled by Brihaspati, means radiance. A birth here gives a graceful, attractive and refined personality with artistic taste, friendliness and good fortune. It is auspicious for ceremonies, new ventures and social occasions.
yoga.Atiganda: Atiganda, ruled by Chandra, is considered an inauspicious yoga. It may give worry, hidden obstacles and a restless mind or quarrelsome tendencies, but awareness and calm habits temper this. It is traditionally avoided for new undertakings.
yoga.Sukarma: Sukarma, ruled by Aditi, means good deeds. It tends to give a virtuous, hardworking and charitable nature, steady reputation and success through honest effort. It is auspicious for righteous work, learning and ritual.
yoga.Dhriti: Dhriti, ruled by Jala, means steadfastness. A birth here gives a patient, determined, content nature, good with commitments and with a tendency toward comfort and stability. It is favourable for lasting agreements and settled plans.
yoga.Shula: Shula, ruled by Sarpa, means a spear. It is a sharp, inauspicious yoga that may give an irritable, argumentative or anxious nature, with tendencies to pain or sudden friction. Self-control and patience soften it, and new ventures are traditionally avoided.
yoga.Ganda: Ganda, ruled by Agni, means a knot. It is inauspicious and may give knots or obstacles in life, a restless or impulsive temperament and entanglements, though awareness helps untie them. It is traditionally avoided for new beginnings.
yoga.Vriddhi: Vriddhi, ruled by the Sun, means growth. A birth here favours progress, increasing wealth, learning and reputation, with a hopeful, enterprising nature. It is auspicious for investments, new ventures and anything meant to grow.
yoga.Dhruva: Dhruva, ruled by Bhumi, means fixed. It gives a steady, reliable, determined character with durable results and good fortune from patient effort. It is favourable for foundations, buildings and long-term commitments.
yoga.Vyaghata: Vyaghata, ruled by Vayu, means a heavy blow. It is traditionally difficult, with a tendency toward harshness, abruptness or hurtful dealings, though discipline and compassion can channel its forcefulness. Auspicious beginnings are best avoided.
yoga.Harshana: Harshana, ruled by Bhaga, means joy. A birth here gives a cheerful, enthusiastic, sociable nature with good fortune and happiness. It is auspicious for celebrations, social gatherings and positive new beginnings.
yoga.Vajra: Vajra, ruled by Varuna, means thunderbolt. It gives a strong, forceful will and resolve, with ability to cut through obstacles, though temper and sudden swings may need care. Results are mixed and best for firm, decisive tasks.
yoga.Siddhi: Siddhi, ruled by Ganesha, means accomplishment. A birth here gives skill, success in endeavours, and a capable, resourceful nature. It is one of the most auspicious yogas for beginning ventures, learning and ritual.
yoga.Vyatipata: Vyatipata, ruled by Rudra, means great calamity. It is considered an inauspicious yoga that may bring sudden disruptions, an unsettled temperament and reversals, though awareness softens them. Auspicious beginnings are traditionally avoided.
yoga.Variyan: Variyan, ruled by Kubera, means comfort. A birth here gives a taste for comfort, luxury and prosperity, with ability to gather resources and enjoy them. It is generally favourable though self-indulgence should be moderated.
yoga.Parigha: Parigha, ruled by Vishvakarma, means an iron bar. It is inauspicious and can indicate blocked progress, opposition or obstacles, along with a stubborn streak. It strengthens persistence, but new ventures are traditionally avoided.
yoga.Shiva: Shiva, ruled by Mitra, is auspicious. A birth here gives a spiritual, gentle, helpful and fortunate nature, with a good reputation and the blessings of elders. It supports worship, learning and positive new beginnings.
yoga.Siddha: Siddha, ruled by Kartikeya, means accomplished. It gives competence, achievement and the ability to fulfil goals, along with a disciplined and capable nature. It is excellent for undertakings, study and spiritual practice.
yoga.Sadhya: Sadhya, ruled by Savitri, means achievable. A birth here gives a practical, perseverant nature that gets things done, with success in sustained effort and some talent for ritual or learning. It is generally favourable.
yoga.Shubha: Shubha, ruled by Lakshmi, means auspicious. It gives a pleasant, benevolent and refined nature with good fortune, reputation and material comfort. It is favourable for ceremonies, new ventures and harmonious work.
yoga.Shukla: Shukla, ruled by Parvati, means bright. A birth here gives a pure, clear, bright and generous nature, with good learning, honesty and the support of others. It is auspicious for study, worship and wholesome endeavours.
yoga.Brahma: Brahma, ruled by Ashvini Kumaras, is a wise and creative yoga. It gives intelligence, a balanced temperament, spiritual interest and skill in guiding others. It is favourable for study, healing and constructive beginnings.
yoga.Indra: Indra, ruled by Pitris, gives leadership, courage, authority and ambition. A birth here suggests a capable, commanding character, strong in public life and often respected. Pride should be balanced with generosity.
yoga.Vaidhriti: Vaidhriti, ruled by Diti, means separation. It is traditionally inauspicious, linked with disruption, separation or obstacles, and may give a conflicted temperament; conscious steadiness helps. Auspicious beginnings are best avoided.

karana.Bava: Bava is a movable karana ruled by Indra. It is favourable, giving a cheerful, energetic, ambitious nature and good results in most undertakings, especially those involving learning, leadership and general activity.
karana.Balava: Balava is a movable karana ruled by Brahma. It is favourable, giving a gentle, scholarly, strong and religious nature, and it supports ritual, study, ceremonies and constructive activities.
karana.Kaulava: Kaulava is a movable karana ruled by Mitra. It gives a friendly, cooperative and sociable nature, and it is good for building friendships, partnerships, alliances and community matters.
karana.Taitila: Taitila is a movable karana ruled by Aryaman. It gives a gracious, generous and prosperous nature, with good fortune in worldly matters, and it supports property, social occasions and steady progress.
karana.Garaja: Garaja is a movable karana ruled by Bhumi. It gives hardworking, practical habits, with success through agriculture, property and steady effort, and it supports work needing persistence.
karana.Vanija: Vanija is a movable karana ruled by Lakshmi. It gives a talent for trade, negotiation and business, and it supports commerce, dealings with money and enterprise.
karana.Vishti: Vishti, also called Bhadra, is a movable karana ruled by Yama. It is considered inauspicious for new beginnings and ceremonies, giving a stubborn or forceful nature, though suited to confronting enemies and tough work.
karana.Shakuni: Shakuni is a fixed karana ruled by the Kali force. It gives a shrewd, clever and cautious mind with interests in medicine, strategy and healing, and it suits remedies and diplomacy rather than ceremonies.
karana.Chatushpada: Chatushpada is a fixed karana ruled by Rudra. It is linked with animals, cattle and ancestral rites, and it suits worship of ancestors and animal husbandry, while being less suited to new ventures.
karana.Naga: Naga is a fixed karana ruled by Sarpa. It gives a secretive, shrewd and intense nature, and it suits ancestral rites and remedies for serpent-related matters, while being unsuited to new auspicious ventures.
karana.Kimstughna: Kimstughna is a fixed karana ruled by Vayu, occurring at the start of Shukla Pratipada. It is gentle and supports spiritual practice and prayer, while being considered not especially strong for business or major starts.

vara.Sunday: Sunday is ruled by the Sun. A birth on this day is associated with dignity, leadership, vitality and a strong sense of self, with a natural pull toward authority, government and recognition. It favours worship of the Sun and health-building habits.
vara.Monday: Monday is ruled by the Moon. A birth on this day gives a sensitive, caring and imaginative temperament, with emotional intelligence, public appeal and attachment to home. It favours water-related work, nurturing activities, and calming practices.
vara.Tuesday: Tuesday is ruled by Mars. A birth on this day suggests courage, energy, a competitive streak and practical skill, with a risk of impatience. It favours courageous action, physical effort, land matters and disciplined, focused work.
vara.Wednesday: Wednesday is ruled by Mercury. A birth on this day gives a quick, curious and communicative mind, with skill in learning, speech, trade and writing. It favours study, commerce, travel, contracts and work that needs flexibility.
vara.Thursday: Thursday is ruled by Jupiter. A birth on this day gives a wise, generous and principled nature, with respect for teachers, learning and traditions. It favours education, ceremonies, advice, beginnings of virtuous work and charity.
vara.Friday: Friday is ruled by Venus. A birth on this day gives a charming, artistic and pleasure-loving nature, with appreciation for beauty, relationships and comfort. It favours marriage, arts, finance, vehicles and gentle social undertakings.
vara.Saturday: Saturday is ruled by Saturn. A birth on this day gives a serious, patient and hardworking character, with endurance and responsibility, and a path that often matures later. It favours steady labour, discipline, service and long-term projects.
